Install SCGSim into your study project with `uv` from the source revision documented here. SCGSim requires Python `>=3.12,<3.14`; `uv` manages the project environment in `.venv` and records resolved dependencies in `uv.lock`.

## Create a study project

1. Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git. Git lets `uv` fetch SCGSim from its source repository.

   Check: `uv --version` and `git --version` print installed versions.

2. Create a project and add SCGSim with the Palace preparation tools. This uses package version `2.0.0rc11` from source commit `90fb50ef9de80fa6e556d2f2a09fb45707efeea0`.

   ```bash
   uv init --python 3.12 scgsim-study
   cd scgsim-study
   uv add 'scgsim[palace] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@90fb50ef9de80fa6e556d2f2a09fb45707efeea0'
   ```

   Use `--python 3.13` if that is the interpreter selected for the study. For project setup details, see the [uv project guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/) and its [Git dependency syntax](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/dependencies/#git).

   Check: `uv run python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('scgsim'))"` prints `2.0.0rc11`.

3. Keep `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` with the study. On another computer, run `uv sync` in the project folder to recreate its environment from the lock file.

   ```bash
   uv sync
   ```

   Check: the same `uv run` version command prints `2.0.0rc11`.

## Select backend tools

The base package supplies NumPy and Plotly for resolving and plotting returned results. Add the extras needed for your calculation.

| Extra | Use | Python packages supplied |
|---|---|---|
| `palace` | Prepare Palace geometry, mesh and configuration | GDSFactory 9, `gdstk`, Gmsh |
| `aedt` | Prepare ordinary HFSS or Q3D models; use Q2D | `gdstk`, PyAEDT 1.3.0 |
| `aedt-epr` | Prepare source-first AEDT surface EPR models | AEDT dependencies, GDSFactory 9 and KLayout 0.30.x |
| `visualization` | Inspect solver-bound geometry | `meshio`, Pillow and PyVista; combine with the backend extra |

Use `uv add --extra` to select the extras from the pinned SCGSim source. This example includes both SimplePad beginner backend paths:

```bash
uv add --extra palace --extra aedt-epr --extra visualization \
  'scgsim @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@90fb50ef9de80fa6e556d2f2a09fb45707efeea0'
```

Check: `uv run python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('scgsim'))"` prints `2.0.0rc11` after `uv` updates the environment.

## Open a notebook

Choose a goal from the [simulation chooser](../examples.qmd), then run that tutorial's exact PDK `uv add` command in this study project before launching Jupyter. Each tutorial pins the public component source for its workflow.

Start Jupyter through `uv` from the study project. This runs it with the project's Python environment.

```bash
uv run --with jupyter jupyter lab
```

For details, see [Using uv with Jupyter](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/jupyter/).

Check: Jupyter opens from the study project and its notebook uses that project's Python environment.

### Select the curved source cell {#select-the-curved-source-cell}

The Circular Pad source and its separate pinned environment are documented in the [historical curved-source setup](../history/curved-source-installation.qmd).

## Install the native solver separately

Python extras supply Python libraries. Install native Palace 0.18.1 from its [official release](https://github.com/awslabs/palace/releases/tag/v0.18.1) on the solver host. For AEDT, use AEDT 2023.2 or 2024.2 with PyAEDT 1.3.0 and a suitable license. Select the AEDT release explicitly in each request; each AEDT Desktop transaction runs on the same host as SCGSim.

Check: confirm the Palace executable or wrapper, or the selected AEDT release and license, are available on the solver host before running the calculation.

#### Native Palace for this curved Uniform port {#native-palace-for-this-curved-uniform-port}

The [historical curved-source setup](../history/curved-source-installation.qmd#native-palace-for-this-curved-uniform-port) records the native Palace prerequisite for that specific study.
